priorStatuses.title: Handle missing cache entries before trimming

findings.title: [P1] Do not log issued authentication tokens
findings.body: Whenever `recordIssuedToken` receives a live bearer or session token, it passes the complete credential to `console.log` through `audit`. Persisted or aggregated logs would expose replayable credentials to anyone with log access.

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted local destinations
findings.body: If `returnUrl` can be influenced by a login request, `location.assign` accepts absolute and protocol-relative external URLs. This changes the fixed internal redirect into an open redirect that can send authenticated users to an attacker-controlled site; require a same-origin path or an allowlisted destination.

findings.title: [P1] Redact issued tokens before auditing
findings.body:
Every token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is sent verbatim to `console.log` through `audit`. When used with real bearer/session tokens in an environment that captures stdout, credentials are exposed to logs and anyone with log access.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued authentication tokens to logs
findings.body:
Every call passes the raw issued token to console.log via audit. Production consoles are commonly persisted or aggregated, exposing bearer credentials to log readers and enabling account impersonation until those tokens expire or are revoked.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted local destinations
findings.body:
location.assign accepts absolute and protocol-relative URLs, so an attacker-controlled returnUrl can send authenticated users to an external site. The previous implementation always used a fixed internal destination; validate against an allowlist or accept only same-origin paths.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not log issued tokens in plaintext
findings.body:
Every call with a live authentication token writes that credential to stdout. In deployments where logs are collected or accessible to operators/services, anyone with log access can replay the token and impersonate its holder.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
